reviewA: As a lyric reader, I am looking for compression and language that does work on the page. Post A succeeds through a highly specific lexical invention. The author translates the abstract computational physics of the Ruliad into the vocabulary of the Pantanal. 'Cada escolha é um galho que a gente não viu crescer / Bifurcando no destino antes mesmo de chover' is an excellent, grounded image of branching multiversal paths that avoids sci-fi clichés. The nouns do the heavy lifting: 'Tulha' (silo) for the space of all computations, 'Moagem' for the processing of reality. 'A conta dessa estrada se faz no pisar do chão' is a strong line that anchors the high-concept theory. There are some filler lines forced by the 'toada' rhyme scheme ('no espaço sideral / no processamento final' feels a bit clunky), but overall the lyrics survive the page by creating a coherent, localized mythology for a metaphysical problem.
reviewB: Post B presents a text that the composer explicitly admits 'was not written to be a song lyric.' Stripped of the music, it reads not as poetry, but as a manic, ecstatic prose poem driven by alliteration. The compression is entirely absent. Instead of density, we get a deluge: 'autônomo, autóctone, autopotente, autocatalítico, autopoético.' This is not a line doing the work of a paragraph; this is a thesaurus performing a ritual. The sound texture is certainly not incidental, but it feels forced rather than inevitable. It relies heavily on a pseudo-shamanic, high-register vocabulary ('pandemia poética,' 'delírio lírico,' 'líquido lingham do logos') that comes across as exhausting rather than evocative on the page. The composer notes admit to the excess, but acknowledging a flaw does not fix the poem. It is a text that requires the hypnotic music to mask its lack of restraint.
clash: Which lyrics earn the page, not just the performance? Post A takes a highly complex abstract idea and forces it through the constraint of regional vocabulary, producing startling, compressed images like 'Grão-de-Lógica brotando nas veredas do capim.' It earns its place as poetry because the friction between the subject and the language creates new meaning. Post B, however, abandons constraint entirely. It substitutes density with volume, piling up alliterations and esoteric vocabulary until the lines collapse under their own weight. On the page, Post B is exhausting to read, a maximalist exercise that lacks the discipline of a true lyric. Post A uses words to build a structure; Post B uses words as an aesthetic avalanche. Post A, 4.10 to 3.20.
